subject: mathematics
question_text: If f: R→R and g: R→R are defined by f(x) = 3x − 2 and g(x) = x² + 1, find (gof)(x − 1).

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.10, chapter 2 FUNCTIONS, Very Short Answer question 8(ii). Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1 shape gives one mark to the inner value f(x − 1) = 3x − 5 and one to the expansion, because the order of composition and the squaring of a bracket are the two separate skills being tested. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1–Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find (gof)(x − 1) — which function acts first, and what it acts on.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Work f at x − 1
steps.margin_note: First mark. The input is x − 1, not x. Getting f(x − 1) = 3x − 5 on the page earns this mark on its own, even if the expansion afterwards slips.
steps.memory_tip: In gof, g is outside and f is inside, so f meets the input x − 1 first.
lines: f acts first, at the input x − 1:

recall.must_convey: That in gof the inner function is f, so f is worked at x − 1 first, giving 3x − 5.
accept: in g o f the inner function is f so first find f of x minus one which is three x minus five
f of x minus one is three times x minus one minus two that is three x minus five
work f first because it is written second and acts first
modata f of x minus one teeskovali adi three x minus five
the inner function f gives three x minus five

steps.why: In gof the function written on the right acts first, and here its input is the whole of x − 1. Writing f(x − 1) = 3x − 5 fixes what g will receive.
common_mistakes: Applying g first, which computes (fog)(x − 1) and gives a different expression.
Writing 3(x − 1) − 2 as 3x − 1 by multiplying only the x by 3.

steps.label: Apply g and expand
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The whole bracket is squared, so the expansion has three terms. The + 1 that belongs to g is added after the expansion.
steps.memory_tip: (3x − 5)² = 9x² − 2(3x)(5) + 25. The middle term −30x is the one students drop.

recall.must_convey: That g squares 3x − 5 and adds 1, giving 9x² − 30x + 26.
accept: g of three x minus five is three x minus five all squared plus one
expand to nine x squared minus thirty x plus twenty five then add one
the answer is nine x squared minus thirty x plus twenty six
three x minus five whole square plus one ante nine x squared minus thirty x plus twenty six
square the bracket and add one to get twenty six as the constant
heard_as: three x minus five whole squared

steps.why: g squares whatever it is given, so the bracket (3x − 5) must be squared as one quantity. The constant 26 is 25 from the square plus the 1 that g always adds.
common_mistakes: Writing (3x − 5)² as 9x² − 25 or as 9x² + 25, losing the middle term.
Dropping the + 1 that belongs to g and answering 9x² − 30x + 25.
